questions.q: What two things should you examine first when preparing to pivot?
a: Your strengths and your finances
Your age and your credentials
Your network and your salary
Your hobbies and your free time
questions.why: Lesson 1 says to start by reviewing past evaluations and your money, so you know your base and can cover costs.

questions.q: What does the author say you realize once you list your strengths?
a: You are building on expertise, not starting over
You need a completely new qualification
You have been in the wrong field entirely
You should wait for the right moment to move
questions.why: Lesson 1 says the exercise shows your experience is a solid foundation rather than something you are abandoning.

questions.q: Which habit from The 7 Habits does Blake say a pivot requires?
a: Being proactive
Beginning with the end in mind
Putting first things first
Seeking first to be understood
questions.why: Lesson 2 cites proactivity, meaning you take responsibility and act instead of waiting or blaming others.

questions.q: What did the author realize he could do while still at his old job?
a: Earn the same money in a quarter of the time
Train for a new career during work hours
Sell his services to his own employer
Retire early on his existing savings
questions.why: Lesson 2 says doing his day job independently would bring the same income and cut his workday by over 75 percent.

questions.q: What is the purpose of small experiments during a pivot?
a: To test the new career while still earning a living
To prove the old career was the wrong choice
To build a portfolio before applying for jobs
To convince employers that you are serious
questions.why: Lesson 3 says small experiments let you manage risk by keeping your income and seeing how well you like the field.
